tur27-1: No. Despite the name, growing pains have nothing to do with growing and are not a sign of a serious illness. The cause is not known. They are more common in active children and after days with a lot of sport, and are also common in children with joint hypermobility (connective tissue laxity). In a 2022 review of 147 studies, more than 90% of the studies defining growing pains made no mention of growth in their definition.
tur27-2: It is a simple 9-point examination doctors use to assess joint mobility: bending the little finger back more than 90 degrees, touching the thumb to the forearm, the elbow and the knee bending backwards more than 10 degrees (one point each for right and left), and placing the palms flat on the floor with the knees straight (one point). Under the 2017 international criteria, the threshold for generalised joint hypermobility is 6 in children and adolescents, 5 in adults up to 50 and 4 over 50. It is not a self-diagnosis test; the diagnosis is made by a doctor.

tur27-4: School bags, one-sided habits and connective tissue flexibility
tur27-5: In one study, 51.4% of 70 children with idiopathic scoliosis had generalised joint hypermobility (excessive joint mobility due to connective tissue laxity), compared with 19% of healthy peers; laxity was not related to the size of the curve. The authors recommend checking for joint laxity in these children when planning physiotherapy.
tur27-6: In children with very flexible connective tissue, strengthening and posture control come before stretching.
tur27-7: According to research, no: the Scoliosis Research Society (SRS) states that heavy bags, poor posture and sport do not cause scoliosis or make a curve worse, and a study of 966 students in Portugal also found no association between bag weight or posture habits and scoliosis. A heavy bag can, however, cause back pain. In our clinical experience, one-sided loading can make postural asymmetry and pain more pronounced in young people who are in the growth spurt and have flexible connective tissue, so we recommend carrying the bag on both shoulders.
